verdict: The Saboteur Sketchbook is the most structurally ambitious deck in the corpus — 14 thematic sequences flowing from the 1910 Flexner Report through pandemic-era suppression to FrizzleBob's personal exit. The organizational architecture alone earns it a special mention: Founding Architecture → Subscription Model → Five Scandal Sequences → The Eliminated → The Fauna → Clinical Encounter → System's Arsenal → Exit Strategy is a complete documentary in card form. Named strength: the Sickness Subscription Model sequence (cards 5-8) is perfect — 'A cured patient is a catastrophic loss of recurring revenue' belongs in the all-time Kayfabizarro vault. Named weakness: power text on several back-half pages runs small and was partially illegible at table resolution — PDUFA, The Unfilled Prescription, and the mRNA cards lose clarity. Table-ready YES — with a font-size audit on power text recommended.
blurb: For anyone who's ever been told their question was dangerous. The Saboteur Sketchbook deals the full history of pharmaceutical monopoly as a 56-card game — and ends with the one card they cannot regulate.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: MEDICINE MADNESS: THE WAITING ROOM ANARCHY – Play the Full History of Captured Medicine (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

When did asking what is actually in the pill become the dangerous part?

Run the numbers the way the industry runs them. A molecule you can patent earns back a billion-dollar trial. A cheap vegetable, an old generic, a fasting protocol earns nobody anything, so it never gets the trial, so it never gets the evidence, so it stays "unproven" forever by design. That is not a gap in the science. That is the business model working exactly as built. The key opinion leader gets flown to the conference, the inconvenient result gets filed under acceptable business risk, and the person who actually recovered becomes a number nobody is paid to publish.

Medicine Madness deals that machine as a game you run with your own hands. This is Social Story Wrestling for the waiting room: 56 cut-and-play cards and fourteen scandals deep, a roster you perform out loud until the table decides whether the cover story holds or gets exposed mid-sentence.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Medicine Madness Core Deck: 56 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring The Key Opinion Leader Parrot, the expert who repeats whatever the last grant told him, The Unpatentable Vegetable, the cure with no margin and therefore no trial, and The Cured Patient, the outcome the system has no billing code for.
- The Freestyle Rules: The complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, no medical degree, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the one law that every card can claim anything, as long as you can sell it before the room calls the work.
- The 14-Scandal Investigation: the deck runs as one continuous case, fourteen named chapters deep, from the early capture of the field to the exit strategy, so you watch organized medicine get bought one chapter at a time. It ends on Frances Oldham Kelsey, the regulator who looked at the data and said no, the one card they could never quite regulate.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
You are not buying a static PDF. You are buying into the Dark Journalism cycle. Every future chapter, every new scandal folded into this investigation, every sibling deck in the series lands in your library as a free update. The file grows as the case does.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I trained in medicine, and I have watched good questions get relabeled as dangerous ones. This deck hands the whole captured history back to you as a toy you are allowed to break. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Read it, print it, run the racket yourself at the kitchen table until you can spot the move in the wild. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the next comic cards and sharper mechanics.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
They can patent the molecule. They can never patent the question.
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
